photos.c: Stroll In The Park By Gittins
Harry Churcher finishes 5th in the final of the 10,000m Walk at the 1948 Olympics held in London.

To 29th January 1938 and the Belgrave 10 miles walking championship. Our picture shows J.Coleman (2nd), P.Wright (3rd), H.Churcher (1st) and L.Coleman (4th) slugging it out for the lead along Southside.

This photograph is part of the complete one taken at the Belgrave 50th Anniversary Dinner 1937 and shows as numbered some of the club's race walkers of that period. No 7 is Harold King (see obituary notice) others are 1. Chas Churcher, 2. Harry Churcher, 3. Joe Coleman, 4. Tommy Green, 5. Jack Bidgood and 6. Frank Elson.
Belgrave's leading walker of 1946 was Harry Churcher. He went on to take 5th place in the 10,000 metres Walk at the 1948 Wembley Olympics.

Wimbledon Common c.1950, with Len Coleman (far left) and Harry Churcher (second from right) race walking four abreast along The Causeway with not the slightest need to worry about the traffic. Photographer unknown.

The caption that goes with this photograph in our archives reads:
"Walk Match at Battersea circa 1938. Starters include H.G. Churcher, C.E.Churcher, D.E. Brown, A.A.Harley, F. Jarvis, C.W.Redgrave."
Our first stab at actually naming the faces came up with Don Brown (1), Harry Churcher (7), Charlie Churcher (23), C.W. Redgrave (24) and Alf Harley (behind Brown). However, as others have become involved and have cast their eyes over the picture, we are now not at all sure of anyone except Alf Harley. For instance, we are told that Charlie Churcher did not wear glasses and the chap next to Harry, second from the left, may be Jack Rutland If any reader can help us with more specific details of the race then we would be very pleased to hear from them.
